# c9s

> Terminal dashboard for Claude Code. c9s is a k9s-inspired TUI that shows every Claude Code session across every project in a single view. It reads directly from `~/.claude/` (no daemon, no API, no network beyond an optional OAuth usage check), runs each session in its own tmux window, and surfaces live status (processing / waiting / done) via Claude Code hooks. Single Go binary plus tmux; MIT-licensed; macOS and Linux.

c9s targets developers who run many concurrent Claude Code sessions and lose track of which one is waiting for input, which one is streaming, and which one they left half-finished yesterday. If you have used k9s for Kubernetes, the model is the same: a keyboard-driven table, cheap to launch, kills the need to hunt through terminals.

Non-goals worth stating up front: c9s does not proxy Claude Code, does not orchestrate multi-agent workflows, does not send data anywhere. Live status is powered by official Claude Code hooks that write a small per-session state file under `~/.c9s/state/`; nothing hits the network unless you explicitly turn on the optional ntfy.sh phone-notification forwarder.

## Docs

- [Homepage](https://stefanoguerrini.dev/c9s/): one-page overview with install commands and the animated demo
- [README](https://github.com/StefanoGuerrini/c9s#readme): full reference covering features, keybindings, session and pane status semantics, worktree hierarchy, API usage tracking, and configuration
- [Releases](https://github.com/StefanoGuerrini/c9s/releases): tagged versions with changelog and prebuilt binaries for darwin/linux × amd64/arm64
- [Issues](https://github.com/StefanoGuerrini/c9s/issues): bug reports and feature requests
- [Source](https://github.com/StefanoGuerrini/c9s): repository root

## Install

- Homebrew: `brew install stefanoguerrini/tap/c9s`
- Go: `go install github.com/stefanoguerrini/c9s@latest`
- Source: `git clone https://github.com/stefanoguerrini/c9s && cd c9s && go build -o c9s .`

Run `c9s` from any shell. It auto-creates a tmux session and attaches, or re-attaches if one is already running. `c9s --demo` shows the dashboard with fake data.

Live pane status requires one setup step: `c9s install` merges the required Claude Code hooks into `~/.claude/settings.json`. `c9s uninstall` removes them cleanly.

## Core concepts

- **Session**: one Claude Code conversation, identified by a session ID and backed by a JSONL file under `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<id>.jsonl`.
- **Session lifecycle status**: `active` (JSONL modified in the last five minutes) / `idle` (claude process running) / `resumable` (JSONL exists on disk) / `archived` (only in history).
- **Pane status** (managed sessions only): `processing` / `waiting` / `done` / `unknown`. Sourced from Claude Code hooks that update a per-session state file c9s reads on every tick.
- **Managed window**: a tmux window c9s opened. c9s tags windows with the session ID so it can adopt them after a restart.
- **Worktree**: c9s discovers git worktrees per project and, when grouping by project, renders a two-level hierarchy (project → worktree → sessions) with per-worktree dirty / ahead / behind indicators. `a` adds a worktree, `d` removes one.

## Keybindings (dashboard)

- Navigate: `j`/`k` or arrows
- Open / resume: `Enter`
- New session: `n` (in the project picker), `N` (chain into the effort picker)
- Close managed window: `x`
- Rename: `R`; backup JSONL: `b`; search: `/`; clear filter: `Esc`
- Cycle grouping: `Tab` (none → project → status)
- Toggle preview panel: `p`; toggle token column: `t`
- Worktrees (only when `groupBy=project` and `worktrees=on`): `w` toggle, `a` add, `d` delete
- Config editor: `c`; usage history: `u`; quit: `q` or `Ctrl+c`

## Configuration

Config lives at `~/.c9s/config.json`. Edit in-app with `c` or by hand. Settable knobs include refresh interval, scroll speed, default work directory, keep-alive behavior on quit, hide-archived filter, desktop notifications (via `c9s install` hooks), optional ntfy.sh phone push, usage-history recording, worktrees on/off, tmux navigation keybindings, and a custom color theme.

## Requirements

- macOS or Linux (tmux does not run natively on Windows)
- tmux 3.7 or newer
- Go 1.24+ only if building from source

## Optional

- [Related project: agent-deck](https://github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck): a more feature-rich multi-agent dashboard
- [Related project: ntm](https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/ntm): tmux session manager for parallel AI coding agents
- [claude-chill](https://github.com/davidbeesley/claude-chill): PTY proxy that wraps Claude's output in synchronized frames (helps if you see flickering)
- [Ghostty](https://ghostty.org/): terminal with native synchronized output; another flicker-mitigation path
